study type: Secondary analysis of cross-sectional survey data
exposure: number of daughters in a household
marital status (married and living with a partner)
cohort: The study included women of childbearing age in Nigeria, whose data were collected as part of the 2013 Nigerian Demographic Health Survey (NDHS).
finding: Higher maternal education, Yoruba ethnicity, Christianity, family planning use, higher wealth index, and previous Caesarean birth were associated with lower fertility levels, whereas age at first birth, rural residence, number of daughters, being gainfully employed, being married and living with a partner, and community/household effects contributed to higher fertility.
mod_finding: Previous Caesarean birth was identified as a factor associated with lower fertility levels in Nigeria.
